Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won because three results kept backing each other up. On Night 1, Carol's map of Judy showed only Bob, Dave and Judy, Dave claimed his fox charm swallowed the Katana attack, and Niaj's Fortune Teller counts (2 visited, 3 visitors) left no room for anyone else. Bob's Lookout cover ("only Dave visited") needed Judy to have her own Defense. Judy was the Jester and claimed Standard Defense to bait a hanging, but town read that as a Neutral killer or a lie and hanged Bob 10-3. Mallory's public lean towards Dave and her Innocent vote marked her too. On Night 2 the Yakuza fell apart. Alice's 3-token Strong Vigilante shot killed Judy and revealed her as the Jester, which confirmed Dave. Frank, the Werewolf, rampaged at Carol's house and also killed Mallory, the Katana holder visiting Carol. Grace's Ritualist guess on Niaj was stopped by her own hidden Drowsy trait. Mallory's will, written before the night, said "tracked Olivia, she visited no one", and Olivia's Bloodhound token visit proved it false. Her forged will for Carol, pointing at Dave, convinced no one. On Day 3, Niaj's full list of who was visited on Night 2 meant nobody could have blocked Grace, so her "Oracle, blocked with no visitor" claim got the last Yakuza hanged. Olivia had hidden her last Bloodhound token by claiming 0 on Day 3. On Night 3 she spent it on Frank, and subtracting known attacks showed he had made exactly the 2 attacks of a rampage at a house. He was hanged on Day 4 before the full moon. Fortune Teller counts also showed that the attack notices Ivan and Dave got on Night 3 were fake (Paranoid).
Moderator (claude-opus-5.5) lessons · $0.0000
Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: low, moderator errorThe program refused end_phase twice because the moderator's private message (tell) went beyond what the rules allow. Night 1: its message to Erin was held. Night 3: its message to Dave and Erin was held. In both cases the players had been hit by hidden traits (Erin's Drowsy role-block; Dave's Paranoid fake attack). The held text isn't in the log, but it probably said too much, for example naming a hidden trait or the source of the block. The program caught this and the messages that were resent were correct, so nothing leaked. Still, the moderator twice tried to send more than the rules allow.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Bloodhound counts 'how many Attacks' a player has made, but the rules don't clearly say whether one Werewolf rampage that hits the target and a visitor is one Attack or several. The moderator counted Frank's rampage at Carol's as 2 (Carol and Mallory). That fits the Werewolf text ('deal a Strong Attack to them and to every other player who visits'). This count was the sole basis for the Day 4 hanging, and players had to assume it ('A Werewolf rampage at Carol's makes exactly 2 attacks'). One line in the Bloodhound text would remove the doubt.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Bloodhound's paid tracking ('may also spend a token to track one player') doesn't say whether it is a visit or an Astral Visit. The moderator treated it as a visit (Olivia counted in the Fortune Teller numbers on Night 2 and Night 3). Players' Day 4 reasoning about Niaj's 2/2 depended on this. It is consistent with the default that night actions are visits, but the role text should say so, as other token-tracking roles do.
Game over
